definitions.explanation: Kansai dialect equivalent of だめ (dame), indicating something is no good, unacceptable, or impossible.
Used to express prohibition or that something should not be done.

examples.japanese: この{機械|きかい}、もうあかんわ。
examples.english: This machine is no good anymore.

examples.japanese: ここでタバコ{吸|す}ったらあかんで。
{今日|きょう}は{体調|たいちょう}があかんねん。

notes:
DIALECT:
Kansai ({関西|かんさい}) dialect, widely used throughout the region.

ORIGIN:
From {埒|らち}が{明|あ}かぬ (rachi ga akanu - "the fence won't open," meaning no progress), contracted to あかん.

STANDARD EQUIVALENT:
だめ / いけない (standard Japanese)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜したらあかん - must not do ~
・〜せんとあかん - must do ~
・あかんわ - it's no good (emphatic)
・あかんかった - was no good (past)
・あかんやん - it's no good, isn't it

IDIOMATIC:
・もうあかん - I give up / It's hopeless
・あかん{子|こ}ほどかわいい - The worse the child, the more you love them

NOTE:
One of the most recognizable Kansai expressions, frequently heard in media and comedy.
